HEADLINE: More than one million Lula supporters rally on eve of Brazilian election runoff
STANDFIRST: Nearly 159 million people to head to polls on Sunday in battle between leftwing incumbent and Flavio Bolsonaro

THE CROWD FIGURE AND ITS PROVENANCE — IMPORTANT
- The Guardian states in its own voice: "More than one million supporters of Brazil's leftwing president, Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, have streamed on to Rio's most famous beach". The one-million figure is NOT attributed to police, to the organisers, or to any independent count. It is the Guardian's own unattributed estimate.
- "red-clad crowds packed the 2.5-mile Copacabana beach".
- The only person quoted making a size claim is a SUPPORTER, not an official: Josias Silva, a 61-year-old truck driver, said: "There's never been a demonstration like this one. This is the biggest protest in the history of Brazil. And we are going to win tomorrow with more than 60% of the votes." That is a partisan claim, not an estimate.
- TWO SEPARATE RALLIES, which explains much of the divergence: "On Saturday afternoon, Lula attended an even larger rally on Paulista Avenue, in the heart of Brazil's biggest city, Sao Paulo." So Copacabana (Rio) and Paulista Avenue (Sao Paulo) are distinct events on the same day.

ELECTORATE FIGURES (CONFLICT, do not average)
- Guardian, 24 Oct: "Nearly 159m Brazilians will vote in the election's runoff on Sunday".
- Al Jazeera, 4 Oct (first round): "About 160 million registered voters were eligible to cast ballots".

OTHER HARD FACTS
- Bolsonaro led by just under 5% in Minas Gerais in the first round. Minas Gerais has Brazil's second-largest electorate after Sao Paulo. No presidential candidate has ever won the presidency without securing Minas Gerais.
- "Never since the return of democracy to Brazil in the 1980s has the first-round loser managed to bounce back."
- "Lula's Army" is a 10 million-member WhatsApp group created after the first round.
- Bolsonaro supporters gathered in Praca da Liberdade, Belo Horizonte.
- Activists at Copacabana unfurled a banner reading: "WE ARE GOING TO TURN THIS AROUND!"

NAMED QUOTES
- Marta Moraes, 59, restaurateur, in Rio: "We've nothing against the right ... what we're against is Bolsonarismo." And: "I lost four members of my family because of Bolsonaro's neglect."
- Cammy Marinho, 49, DJ and activist: "I'm here to prevent democracy becoming extinct - which is what the Bolsonaro family wants".
- Isabella Gaze, 64, retired teacher: "Being a soldier in Lula's army ... means fighting for Brazilian democracy. This isn't a normal election."
